name: Saner.AI
tagline: AI workspace for capturing, connecting, and querying personal knowledge

pricing.freeTierCaps: 30 AI messages/month, 100 notes, 1 MB per PDF, 100 MB storage and 30 AI requests/month
pricing.billingTerms: monthly only; no annual plan published
pricing.hiddenCosts: Standard's 'unlimited' AI messages are subject to fair use, but the official page does not publish a numeric threshold. Daily AI-request caps remain 30 on Starter and 100 on Standard.

verdictSummary: The visible AI personal knowledge loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Saner.AI earns its keep through polish, sync, importers, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local-first AI personal knowledge app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whyPeopleStillPay: Saner.AI: People pay for a writing surface they trust for years, plus migration tools, sync, and tiny interaction details that disappear into habit.
ongoingBurden: Own schema migrations, backups, sync conflicts, export compatibility, and long-term file readability.

priorArt.name: AppFlowy
priorArt.desc: Local-first open-source workspace with documents and databases.

priorArt.name: Logseq
priorArt.desc: Open-source local knowledge graph and outliner.

alternatives.name: Atomic
alternatives.desc: Capture, automatic connections and cited chat over your notes; bring the model yourself.

facts.install: Download the macOS/Windows/Linux desktop release, use Atomic Cloud, or self-host its three-service Docker Compose stack
facts.engines: Ollama, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible model/embedding endpoint, with separate choices for embeddings, tagging, wiki generation and chat
facts.dataFormat: Knowledge is stored as Markdown 'atoms' plus tags, chunks and sqlite-vec embeddings in Atomic's local/server data directory; cloud users keep that database on Atomic's hosted service, and cloud-model calls send relevant text to the provider
facts.gapVsPaid: It covers capture, links, and cited chat, but its mobile capture, integrations, and overall polish are less mature than Saner.AI's managed workspace.
facts.setupBlocker: The desktop binary installs cleanly, but first-run setup cannot finish without an embedding and generation backend, either an API key or Ollama plus downloaded models

alternatives.name: Khoj
alternatives.desc: Search and chat across personal files, now self-host only because the cloud shut down.

facts.install: Use the hosted app, or self-host the server with Docker or pip and optionally install its desktop/browser/Obsidian clients
facts.engines: Local OpenAI-compatible servers such as Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or vLLM, plus OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini and other cloud APIs
facts.dataFormat: Hosted accounts store chats and indexed documents in Khoj's cloud; self-hosting stores application data and vector embeddings in the operator's PostgreSQL/pgvector database while original synced files remain at their source
facts.gapVsPaid: It is strongest at searching and chatting over existing files, not Saner.AI's frictionless capture and automatic visual connection of new knowledge.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted app is immediate, but private self-hosting requires Docker or Python, PostgreSQL/pgvector, model configuration and an initial document index

alternatives.name: Open Notebook
alternatives.desc: A private source notebook with search and chat; capture is upload-first, not frictionless.

facts.install: Download the official Docker Compose file, set an encryption key, and start the Open Notebook and SurrealDB containers
facts.engines: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini/Vertex, OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Azure/OpenAI-compatible services and local Ollama; optional speech providers for podcast generation
facts.dataFormat: Notebook metadata, notes, source records and encrypted provider credentials live in the self-hosted SurrealDB; uploaded source files live in the mounted notebook_data directory, with selected context sent to any cloud AI provider used
facts.gapVsPaid: It is an upload-first source notebook, so quick capture, automatic connections, and everyday personal-knowledge workflows are weaker than Saner.AI's.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker and 4 GB RAM are required, and the user must replace default secrets then configure at least one model provider or add an Ollama container

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Saner.AI is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Saner.AI, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a local-first AI personal knowledge app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: native mobile clients; conflict-safe multi-device sync; mature importers and exporters.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
